text: three categories can also modelled together cumulative probit (proportional odds) model, fitted ordinal::clmm(). R2_model() handle models, lamb-level R² easy compute hand Piepho’s formulas: latent residual variance 1 (probit), fixed share bias-corrected variance linear predictor, sire share sire variance times factor unequal family sizes. Piepho (2023, Table 5) gives 6.75% (fixed), 4.18% (random) 10.93% (total) model.
code: Footshape_long <- Footshape_binomial %>%   select(yr, b1, b2, b3, sire, k1, k2, k3) %>%   pivot_longer(c(k1, k2, k3), names_to = "category", values_to = "count") %>%   uncount(count) %>%   mutate(category = factor(category, ordered = TRUE))  mod_ord <- ordinal::clmm(category ~ yr + b1 + b2 + b3 + (1 | sire), data = Footshape_long,                          link = "probit", nAGQ = 10)  n <- nrow(Footshape_long) X <- scale(as.matrix(Footshape_long[c("yr", "b1", "b2", "b3")]), scale = FALSE) b <- mod_ord$beta fixed <- (sum((X %*% b)^2) - sum(diag(crossprod(X) %*% vcov(mod_ord)[names(b), names(b)]))) / (n - 1) sizes <- table(Footshape_long$sire) sire <- as.numeric(ordinal::VarCorr(mod_ord)$sire) * (n - sum(sizes^2) / n) / (n - 1) round(100 * c(Fixed = fixed, Random = sire, Total = fixed + sire) / (fixed + sire + 1), 2) ##  Fixed Random  Total  ##   6.75   4.18  10.93

R2_model(fit_grp("probit")) #> # Adjusted R2 for mixed models (Piepho) #>            Total            Fixed           Random Treatment:Clinic  #>           77.90%            5.00%           72.90%            0.05%  #>           Clinic  #>           72.84%  #>  #> Advice: #> i For a non-gaussian model the R2 is on the link (latent) scale: not #>   comparable with an lm R2 or across families and links; use it to compare #>   models of the same family. R2_model(fit_grp("cloglog")) #> # Adjusted R2 for mixed models (Piepho) #>            Total            Fixed           Random Treatment:Clinic  #>           72.63%            3.54%           69.09%            0.00%  #>           Clinic  #>           69.09%  #>  #> Advice: #> ! The fit is singular: a variance estimated as zero gives no share to its #>   random effect, so the random part of R2 may be understated. Consider #>   simplifying the random effects. #> i For a non-gaussian model the R2 is on the link (latent) scale: not #>   comparable with an lm R2 or across families and links; use it to compare #>   models of the same family.

title: Contrasts, joint tests and slopes
text: contrast_family() builds standard sets contrasts among means term, coefficients names emmeans: "pairwise", "revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl", "consec", "poly", "eff" "del.eff". result goes contrastmeans(). nitrogen level nitrogen (Dunnett’s comparisons), exact Dunnett adjustment: Linear quadratic trends nitrogen within variety (), integer orthogonal polynomial coefficients (nitrogen levels equally spaced): result prints table; .data.frame() ($contrasts) returns unrounded, p.value unadjusted p.adj adjusted. 1.x table (rounded, adjusted p-value Pr(>|t|)) still first element, [[1]]. specify_contrast() (see getting-started vignette) writes contrast names means.

title: Overview of predictmeans
text: Mixed-effects models needed split-plot experiments, repeated measurements, meta-analysis many designs. packages fit (‘nlme’, ‘lme4’, ‘glmmTMB’) give model coefficients ANOVA table, inference study usually reports: predicted means, standard errors, confidence intervals multiple comparisons. Permutation tests need distributional assumption: suit small samples data normal, assumptions parametric tests doubt. Semiparametric regression combines parametric terms smooth curves surfaces, relationships whose shape known advance. used widely, biology medicine economics. predictmeans provides diagnostics inference models fitted aov, lm, glm, gls, lme, lmer, glmer, glmmTMB gam, semiparametric models (semireg()): predicted means standard errors confidence intervals, contrasts, multiple comparisons, permutation tests, adjusted R-squared, plots. defaults chosen statistical evidence (e.g. Kenward-Roger degrees freedom REML fits), results checked SAS Genstat package tests, adds one-line note fit data call care (advice()). https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=predictmeans

title: Overview of predictmeans
text: Options predictmeans(): pairwise = TRUE compares every pair means unadjusted p-values (adj = "none", default). adj = "BH" compares pairs p-values adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg method (false discovery rate); adj "none" turns comparisons . "tukey", "holm", "bonferroni" others available. meandecr = TRUE sorts mean_table decreasing mean, FALSE increasing mean. Plots drawn result: autoplot(predm_out) (means one LSD bar), type = "bar", type = "ci" (mean confidence limits; data = TRUE adds observations) type = "pvalue". plot(predm_out) draws first. LSD least significant difference chosen adjustment; standard errors differences equal shown range.

code: covariate_out <- covariatemeans(model=mod, modelterm="Drug", covariate="log10Dose") as.data.frame(covariate_out) %>%   select(Drug, log10Dose, response, std.error, response.conf.low, response.conf.high) %>%    mutate_if(is.numeric, round, digits = 4) %>%    rename(Probability=response, LL=response.conf.low, UL=response.conf.high) %>%    arrange(log10Dose, Drug) %>%    DT_df() predictmeans(mod, "Drug", covariate = c(log10Dose = 1), pairwise = TRUE, letter_ci = TRUE)$mean_table ## $Table ##          Drug    Mean      SE  Df LL(86.5%) UL(86.5%) Bk_Mean Bk_LL(86.5%) ## 1    Morphine  0.9711 0.16486 Inf    0.7246    1.2176  0.8342       0.7657 ## 2     Amidone  1.4402 0.20103 Inf    1.1397    1.7408  0.9251       0.8728 ## 3 Phenadoxone  2.6555 0.33079 Inf    2.1610    3.1501  0.9960       0.9847 ## 4   Pethidine -0.0885 0.06973 Inf   -0.1927    0.0158  0.4648       0.4236 ##   Bk_UL(86.5%) LetterGrp ## 1       0.8883       A   ## 2       0.9591       A   ## 3       0.9992        B  ## 4       0.5063         C ##  ## $Note ## [1] "Letter-based representation of pairwise comparisons by overlap of the comparison intervals (LL, UL: mean +/- 1.495 SE, 86.5% intervals): two means differ at significant level '0.05' when their intervals do not overlap (the SEDs differ: approximate, but every pair here agrees with its test)" # one panel per drug (the default) autoplot(covariate_out) # all drugs in one panel autoplot(covariate_out, panel = character(0)) # on the probit (model) scale, without the bands autoplot(covariate_out, scale = "model", panel = character(0), interval = "none")

title: Permutation and bootstrap tests
text: permmodels() two schemes. Freedman–Lane (method = "freedman-lane"; default, method = "auto"). test, model without tested term (pair means: two means equal) gives fitted values residuals; residuals permuted added back fitted values, statistic computed (Freedman Lane 1983). terms keep effects, test term. linear mixed models residuals decorrelated symmetric square root covariance permuted correlated , model refitted permuted data set, variance parameters estimated time (one set refits per term). refit = FALSE instead fixes covariance data fit, turns model linear model refits: much faster, slightly liberal variance parameters rest units (whole plots blocks: 8.6% instead 5% simulation study, 5.0% refits). GLMs GLMMs first linearised fit (working response working variances link scale); GLMM treated working linear mixed model refitted way. Raw (method = "raw", scheme predictmeans 1.x). response (lm, glm) fitted values together decorrelated residuals (mixed models) permuted, model refitted permuted data set. refits kept permlist. scrambles effects terms , tests global null hypothesis; covariate extreme values related tested term rejected true null hypotheses often (6–7% 5% level, 4–5% Freedman–Lane, simulation study; Anderson Legendre 1999 found linear models). lm, aov, lme gls models tables model’s tests Perm_p_value column; classes show statistics permuted (Wald t F covariance data fixed fit).
code: perm <- permmodels(fm, nperm = 199, seed = 1, ncore = 1) perm #>  #> Coefficients of (fixed) effects: #>                            Estimate Std. Error t value Perm_p_value #> (Intercept)                 80.0000     9.1070  8.7844           NA #> nitro0.2                    18.5000     7.6829  2.4079        0.025 #> nitro0.4                    34.6667     7.6829  4.5122        0.005 #> nitro0.6                    44.8333     7.6829  5.8354        0.005 #> VarietyMarvellous            6.6667     9.7150  0.6862        0.545 #> VarietyVictory              -8.5000     9.7150 -0.8749        0.410 #> nitro0.2:VarietyMarvellous   3.3333    10.8653  0.3068        0.765 #> nitro0.4:VarietyMarvellous  -4.1667    10.8653 -0.3835        0.715 #> nitro0.6:VarietyMarvellous  -4.6667    10.8653 -0.4295        0.645 #> nitro0.2:VarietyVictory     -0.3333    10.8653 -0.0307        0.990 #> nitro0.4:VarietyVictory      4.6667    10.8653  0.4295        0.670 #> nitro0.6:VarietyVictory      2.1667    10.8653  0.1994        0.885 #>  #> Note: Perm_p_value of t test is obtained using '199' Freedman-Lane permutations. The smallest attainable p-value is 1/(199 + 1) = 0.005. #>  #> ANOVA: #> Type I F tests (Freedman-Lane permutations; the model refitted to each permuted data set) #>               Df F value Perm_p_value #> nitro          3 37.6857        0.005 #> Variety        2  1.4853        0.260 #> nitro:Variety  6  0.3028        0.925 #>  #> Note: Perm_p_value of F test is obtained using '199' Freedman-Lane permutations. The smallest attainable p-value is 1/(199 + 1) = 0.005. #>  #> Advice: #> ! Only 199 resamples: p-values at the floor (0.005) only say 'as small as #>   can be shown' (Monte Carlo SE about 0.015 at p = 0.05). Use nperm = 999 #>   or more (4999 for reporting); 'seed' makes it reproducible. fm_cars <- lm(mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl), data = mtcars) permmodels(fm_cars, nperm = 999, type = "II", seed = 1) #>  #> Coefficients of (fixed) effects: #>              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) Perm_p_value #> (Intercept)   33.9908     1.8878 18.0056   <1e-04           NA #> wt            -3.2056     0.7539 -4.2521   0.0002        0.001 #> factor(cyl)6  -4.2556     1.3861 -3.0702   0.0047        0.009 #> factor(cyl)8  -6.0709     1.6523 -3.6742    0.001        0.003 #>  #> Note: Perm_p_value of t test is obtained using '999' Freedman-Lane permutations. The smallest attainable p-value is 1/(999 + 1) = 0.001. #>  #> ANOVA: #> Anova Table (Type II tests) #> Response: mpg #>               Sum Sq Df F value Pr(>F) Perm_p_value #> wt          118.2039  1 18.0801 0.0002        0.001 #> factor(cyl)  95.2633  2  7.2856 0.0028        0.005 #> Residuals   183.0586 28                             #>  #> Note: Perm_p_value of F test is obtained using '999' Freedman-Lane permutations. The smallest attainable p-value is 1/(999 + 1) = 0.001.

title: Permutation and bootstrap tests
text: permutations give p-values pairwise comparisons, pairs table legacy p-value matrix. Freedman–Lane pair tested reduced model, pair’s means equal, p-value depend means: contrasts: method = "raw" pairs use refits. adj adjusts permutation p-values p.adjust() method "sidak", max-|t| method Westfall Young (1993), uses correlation comparisons: adj = "tukey" ("mvt") compares pair’s |t| largest |t| family permuted data set (permutation Tukey test), adj = "westfall" step step, powerful. simulation study kept familywise error rate Tukey’s test . permlist, observed t statistics use unadjusted covariance (Kenward–Roger adjustment), permuted ones .
code: pm <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro", permlist = perm, ncore = 1) pm$pairs[, c("level1", "level2", "estimate", "statistic", "p.value", "p.method")] #>   level1 level2   estimate statistic p.value    p.method #> 1      0    0.2 -19.500000 -4.396098   0.005 permutation #> 2      0    0.4 -34.833333 -7.852859   0.005 permutation #> 3    0.2    0.4 -15.333333 -3.456761   0.005 permutation #> 4      0    0.6 -44.000000 -9.919400   0.005 permutation #> 5    0.2    0.6 -24.500000 -5.523302   0.005 permutation #> 6    0.4    0.6  -9.166667 -2.066542   0.055 permutation cm <- contrast_family(Kmatrix(fm, "nitro"), "trt.vs.ctrl") contrastmeans(fm, "nitro", ctrmatrix = cm, permlist = perm)[[1]] #>         Estimate Std. Error t value Permuted Pr(>|t|) lower.CL upper.CL #> 0.2 - 0  19.5000     4.4358  4.3961             0.005  11.2629  27.7371 #> 0.4 - 0  34.8333     4.4358  7.8529             0.005  26.8245  42.8422 #> 0.6 - 0  44.0000     4.4358  9.9194             0.005  35.5097  52.4903 #> attr(,"Note") #> [1] "The permuted p-value is obtained using '199' permutations." pmw <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro", permlist = perm, adj = "westfall",                     ncore = 1) pmw$pairs[, c("level1", "level2", "p.value", "p.adj")] #>   level1 level2 p.value p.adj #> 1      0    0.2   0.005 0.005 #> 2      0    0.4   0.005 0.005 #> 3    0.2    0.4   0.005 0.010 #> 4      0    0.6   0.005 0.005 #> 5    0.2    0.6   0.005 0.005 #> 6    0.4    0.6   0.055 0.055

title: Permutation and bootstrap tests
text: quickest way ask whether random effect needed varcomp(test = TRUE) (lmer, glmer, glmmTMB semireg() fits). row variance-component table tested refitting model one fit without : term dropped, random slope removed ((Days | Subject) (1 | Subject)), covariance set zero. variance tested boundary range, likelihood ratio referred mixtures Self Liang (1987) Stram Lee (1994), SAS PROC GLIMMIX , chi-square, conservative. tested variance model’s random effect gaussian REML fit, exact null distribution Crainiceanu Ruppert (2004) used. reference distribution may inaccurate (term fewer six levels, binary data fewer five observations per level), warning names rows points parametric bootstrap, simulates model without component refits models simulated data set: clearly non-significant test stops 20 simulated statistics reach observed one; significant one uses nboot (999) refits models. simulation seven designs (package sources, dev/sim-vc-defaults.R) default reference never liberal: rejected 0-4.5% data sets without component 5% level. GLMMs conservative (binary data clusters four 0.5%, Poisson 4%, negative binomial 0%), bootstrap nearer 5% found 5-7% real components. default fast first look, safe gaussian models; GLMMs, small data sets, rows warning names p-values near cut-bootstrap worth time (seconds minute per model 999 draws four cores; glmmTMB fits slower). varcomp(test = TRUE) tests row model without ; permlmer(), , compares two nested models user writes.

title: Permutation and bootstrap tests

code: library(predictmeans)   Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)   Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)   fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)   pm <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro:Variety", atvar = "Variety", adj = "tukey")   summary(pm) #> Predicted means for 'nitro:Variety' (lmerMod model; df: Kenward-Roger, Kenward-Roger adjusted SEs) #> Confidence limits: 95% #>  #>  nitro     Variety estimate std.error    df conf.low conf.high group #>      0 Golden Rain    80.00     9.107 16.08    60.70      99.3   A   #>    0.2 Golden Rain    98.50     9.107 16.08    79.20     117.8   AB  #>    0.4 Golden Rain   114.67     9.107 16.08    95.37     134.0    BC #>    0.6 Golden Rain   124.83     9.107 16.08   105.53     144.1     C #>      0  Marvellous    86.67     9.107 16.08    67.37     106.0    A  #>    0.2  Marvellous   108.50     9.107 16.08    89.20     127.8     B #>    0.4  Marvellous   117.17     9.107 16.08    97.87     136.5     B #>    0.6  Marvellous   126.83     9.107 16.08   107.53     146.1     B #>      0     Victory    71.50     9.107 16.08    52.20      90.8    A  #>    0.2     Victory    89.67     9.107 16.08    70.37     109.0    A  #>    0.4     Victory   110.83     9.107 16.08    91.54     130.1     B #>    0.6     Victory   118.50     9.107 16.08    99.20     137.8     B #>  #> 18 pairwise comparisons within each level of Variety. #> SED: min 7.683, mean 7.683, max 7.683 #> LSD (5%, tukey): 20.5 (equal for all pairs) #> p-values: t tests, adjusted by 'tukey'. #> Means sharing a letter are not significantly different at the 5% level within each level of Variety. #> Comparison intervals: mean +/- 1.125 SE (72.3% intervals); means differ at the 5% level when these do not overlap. The 95% confidence limits are not for comparing means.   ggplot2::autoplot(pm)    ggplot2::autoplot(pm, data = TRUE)    ggplot2::autoplot(pm, type = "bar")    ggplot2::autoplot(pm, type = "ci")    ggplot2::autoplot(pm, type = "pvalue")    plot(predictmeans(fm, "nitro:Variety"), xvar = "Variety", group = "nitro")    fl <- lm(log(yield) ~ nitro * Variety, data = Oats)   ggplot2::autoplot(predictmeans(fl, "nitro:Variety"), type = "ci", data = TRUE) #> The response is log(yield): the means are also given back-transformed to the original scale (trans = I for the model scale only).

code: library(predictmeans)   Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)   fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)   # Dunnett: each nitrogen level against no nitrogen, exact adjustment   K <- Kmatrix(fm, "nitro")   if (requireNamespace("mvtnorm", quietly = TRUE)) {     contrastmeans(fm, "nitro", ctrmatrix = contrast_family(K, "trt.vs.ctrl"),                   adj = "mvt")   } #> Contrasts of 'nitro' (95% limits; p.adj: mvt; Kenward-Roger df) #>  contrast estimate std.error df statistic   p.value     p.adj conf.low #>   0.2 - 0    19.50     4.436 45     4.396 6.657e-05 2.200e-04    10.57 #>   0.4 - 0    34.83     4.436 45     7.853 5.649e-10 3.368e-09    25.90 #>   0.6 - 0    44.00     4.436 45     9.919 6.697e-13 8.626e-14    35.07 #>  conf.high adj.conf.low adj.conf.high #>      28.43        8.718         30.28 #>      43.77       24.052         45.62 #>      52.93       33.218         54.78   # linear and quadratic trends in nitrogen within each variety   K2 <- Kmatrix(fm, "nitro:Variety")   cf <- contrast_family(K2, "poly", by = "Variety", max_degree = 2)   contrastmeans(fm, "nitro:Variety", ctrmatrix = cf) #> Contrasts of 'nitro:Variety' (95% limits; p.adj: none; Kenward-Roger df) #>                contrast estimate std.error df statistic   p.value     p.adj #>     Golden Rain: linear  150.667     24.30 45    6.2014 1.568e-07 1.568e-07 #>  Golden Rain: quadratic   -8.333     10.87 45   -0.7670 4.471e-01 4.471e-01 #>      Marvellous: linear  129.167     24.30 45    5.3165 3.186e-06 3.186e-06 #>   Marvellous: quadratic  -12.167     10.87 45   -1.1198 2.688e-01 2.688e-01 #>         Victory: linear  162.167     24.30 45    6.6747 3.099e-08 3.099e-08 #>      Victory: quadratic  -10.500     10.87 45   -0.9664 3.390e-01 3.390e-01 #>  conf.low conf.high #>    101.73   199.601 #>    -30.22    13.551 #>     80.23   178.101 #>    -34.05     9.717 #>    113.23   211.101 #>    -32.38    11.384 #>  #> Advice: #> i 6 contrasts tested without adjustment: some will be significant by #>   chance. Wand's geoadditive model: a thin-plate surface over the plane with the given knots, # and an O'Sullivan spline in depth (their linear terms are added to the fixed effects) mod <- semireg(grade ~ s(xcoord, ycoord, bs = "ztps", xt = list(knots = as.matrix(copperKnots))) +                  s(zcoord, bs = "os", xt = list(knots = seq(80, 120, by = 5))), data = copper) anova(mod)   # fixed effects (Kenward-Roger) and a test of each smooth term #> Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df) #>  #> Response: grade #>                  F Df Df.res  Pr(>F)   #> (Intercept) 1.9416  1   9.89 0.19402   #> xcoord      2.0529  1   9.71 0.18332   #> ycoord      0.1194  1   9.33 0.73730   #> zcoord      5.3331  1 419.35 0.02141 * #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Smooth terms: likelihood ratio tests of variance = 0 (the curve is its straight-line part); #> reference: exact restricted LRT for the only random effect of a gaussian fit, otherwise 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>             term variance logLik logLik.without   LRT  p.value #>  s_xcoord_ycoord  1.74189 -207.2         -245.5 76.56  < 2e-16 #>         s_zcoord  0.05986 -207.2         -234.1 53.72 1.15e-13 #>                       test #>  0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>  0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) semipred(mod, covariate = c("xcoord", "ycoord"))$plt  # \donttest{ # on the log scale, with the pairwise interactions of the coordinates mod2 <- semireg(log(grade) ~ s(zcoord, bs = "os") + s(xcoord, ycoord, bs = "ztps", k = 6) +                   xcoord:ycoord + xcoord:zcoord + ycoord:zcoord, data = copper) semipred(mod2, covariate = "zcoord", trans = exp)$plt  # }

code: data(growthIndiana) # black boys: a mean curve, and each boy's own curve, a straight line (age | idnum) # plus a spline deviation with one variance for all boys gbm <- subset(growthIndiana, male == 1 & black == 1) gbm$idnum <- factor(gbm$idnum) fit <- semireg(height ~ s(age, bs = "os", k = 20, xt = list(range = c(5.5, 20))) +                  (s(age, k = 10, xt = list(range = c(5.5, 20))) | idnum), data = gbm) anova(fit)$smooth       # are the boys' curves straight lines? #>          term  variance    logLik logLik.without       LRT       p.value #> 1       s_age  9.067556 -935.7451      -974.5493  77.60836  6.281850e-19 #> 2 s_age_idnum 18.185045 -935.7451     -1181.2087 490.92720 4.477477e-109 #>                        test #> 1 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 2 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) semipred(fit, "age", "age")$plt  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # (about 30 s: 2257 measurements, 130 boys' curves) # all boys: a common curve and a black-white deviation curve (the contrast curve of # Harezlak, Ruppert and Wand); at which ages do the races differ, and in growth rate? gm <- subset(growthIndiana, male == 1) gm$idnum <- factor(gm$idnum) gm$race <- factor(ifelse(gm$black == 1, "black", "white")) fit2 <- semireg(height ~ s(age, race, bs = "os", k = 20, xt = list(range = c(5.5, 20))) +                   (s(age, k = 10, xt = list(range = c(5.5, 20))) | idnum), data = gm) dif <- semipred(fit2, "race", "age", contr = c("black", "white"), band = "simultaneous") attr(dif$pred_df, "significant") semipred(fit2, "race", "age", deriv = 1)$plt     # growth rates predictmeans(fit2, "race", covariate = c(age = 12))$means } # }

Transformation response (lm aov positive response   transformed formula) Box-Cox power residuals favour: profile likelihood estimate   \(\lambda\) 95% interval (Box Cox, 1964; MASS::boxcox()). Worth look   interval leaves 1 (transformation); note names usual transformation within interval. Equal variances factor: ratio largest smallest standard deviation   residuals within levels, Brown-Forsythe test (ANOVA absolute deviations medians). Spread vs fitted values (gaussian models) Spearman correlation absolute residuals fitted   values; worth look \(|\rho| \ge 0.2\) p < 0.01 (variance grows mean). Dispersion (Poisson, binomial one trial, negative binomial; glm, glmer,   glmmTMB) Pearson chi-square / residual df, 1 variance function right; overdispersion   (ratio > 1.5, p < 0.01) makes SEs small, underdispersion (ratio < 0.7, p < 0.01) large. mixed   models residual df counts variance parameters, approximation. 0/1 response carries information   dispersion; families estimated dispersion (Gamma, quasi) estimate shown. Zero counts (Poisson, negative binomial) observed zeros simulated fitted model   (200 simulations, fixed seed; user's random numbers changed); worth look   (p < 0.01). Separation (binomial) fitted probabilities 0 1, coefficients beyond 10 logit scale   standard errors 50: estimates Wald tests terms unreliable. Balance cells crossed fixed factors: balanced, unbalanced empty cells; unbalanced data   make Type , II III tests differ (see anova.lmerMod, section 'type test'). (Methods are   # found where predictmeans looks for them: in a package's namespace or, as   # here, in the global environment; registerS3method() also works.)   fit_mymodel <- function(formula, data) {     structure(list(fit = lm(formula, data), call = match.call()), class = "mymodel")   }   registerS3method("coef", "mymodel", function(object, ...) coef(object$fit))   registerS3method("vcov", "mymodel", function(object, ...) vcov(object$fit))   registerS3method("terms", "mymodel", function(x, ...) terms(x$fit))   registerS3method("df.residual", "mymodel", function(object, ...) object$fit$df.residual)    Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)   Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)   m <- fit_mymodel(yield ~ Block + nitro*Variety, data = Oats)   predictmeans(m, "nitro")$means #>   nitro  estimate std.error df conf.low conf.high comparison.low #> 1     0  79.38889  3.758096 55  71.8575  86.92028       74.06339 #> 2   0.2  98.88889  3.758096 55  91.3575 106.42028       93.56339 #> 3   0.4 114.22222  3.758096 55 106.6908 121.75362      108.89672 #> 4   0.6 123.38889  3.758096 55 115.8575 130.92028      118.06339 #>   comparison.high  n estimable #> 1        84.71439 18      TRUE #> 2       104.21439 18      TRUE #> 3       119.54772 18      TRUE #> 4       128.71439 18      TRUE    # Degrees of freedom of its own, e.g. normal-based:   registerS3method("pm_df", "mymodel", function(model, L, ...) rep(Inf, nrow(L)))   predictmeans(m, "nitro")$means #>   nitro  estimate std.error  df  conf.low conf.high comparison.low #> 1     0  79.38889  3.758096 Inf  72.02316  86.75462       74.18053 #> 2   0.2  98.88889  3.758096 Inf  91.52316 106.25462       93.68053 #> 3   0.4 114.22222  3.758096 Inf 106.85649 121.58796      109.01386 #> 4   0.6 123.38889  3.758096 Inf 116.02316 130.75462      118.18053 #>   comparison.high  n estimable #> 1        84.59725 18      TRUE #> 2       104.09725 18      TRUE #> 3       119.43058 18      TRUE #> 4       128.59725 18      TRUE

code: library(predictmeans) # a field trial in 6 rows x 6 columns, 3 blocks of 2 rows, with a smooth trend over the field set.seed(1) d <- expand.grid(row = 1:6, col = 1:6) d$block <- factor((d$row + 1) %/% 2) d$variety <- factor(sample(rep(1:6, 6))) d$yield <- 10 + as.numeric(d$variety) + sin(d$row / 2) + cos(d$col / 2) + rnorm(36, sd = 0.3) fm <- lm(yield ~ block + variety, data = d) v <- residvariogram(fm, row = "row", col = "col", nsim = 19, plot = FALSE) v #> Sample variogram of standardized residuals on the row x column grid #> Semivariance relative to the residual variance: about 1 without spatial pattern. #> Global envelope test (95%, 19 simulations from the model): p = 0.05 #>  #> Lags along rows and columns (all 12 lags: as.data.frame(x); the surface: autoplot(x, type = "surface")): #>  lag_row lag_col n_pairs gamma lower upper outside #>        1       0      30 0.331 0.335  1.57    TRUE #>        2       0      24 0.257 0.232  1.60   FALSE #>        0       1      30 0.436 0.433  1.70   FALSE #>        0       2      24 0.690 0.385  1.76   FALSE #>  #> Advice: #> ! Plots next to each other in the same column are more alike than the model #>   allows (the variogram is below the envelope at the shortest lag): the #>   standard errors of the means ignore it. Fit a spatial covariance (AR1 x #>   AR1 in ASReml or Genstat; in R, gls() or lme() with corExp(form = ~ row + #>   col)) or a smooth surface s(row, col) in semireg(), and check its #>   variogram. ggplot2::autoplot(v)

code: library(predictmeans) ## 1. The scallop survey (longitude and latitude): the boundary from the data (blue) and the ##    boundary drawn with the original analysis (red) data(scallop); data(scallopBdry) b <- semiboundary(scallop[, c("longitude", "latitude")]) attr(b, "scale")                                   # "lonlat", from the column names #> [1] "lonlat" plot(latitude ~ longitude, data = scallop, asp = 1/cos(40*pi/180), pch = 16, cex = 0.6,      xlim = range(b$longitude, na.rm = TRUE), ylim = range(b$latitude, na.rm = TRUE)) polygon(b, border = "blue", lwd = 2) polygon(scallopBdry, border = "red", lwd = 2) legend("bottomright", c("semiboundary()", "scallopBdry"), col = c("blue", "red"),        lwd = 2, bty = "n")   ## 2. Copper drill holes (coordinates in the same unit): how 'mult' changes the region; ##    with mult = 1 the hole far to the left is a separate piece data(copper) holes <- unique(copper[, c("xcoord", "ycoord")]) b1 <- semiboundary(holes, mult = 1, scale = "same") b2 <- semiboundary(holes, scale = "same") b4 <- semiboundary(holes, mult = 4, scale = "same") plot(holes, asp = 1, pch = 16, xlim = range(b4$xcoord, na.rm = TRUE),      ylim = range(b4$ycoord, na.rm = TRUE)) polygon(b1, border = "orange", lwd = 2) polygon(b2, border = "blue", lwd = 2) polygon(b4, border = "darkgreen", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("mult = 1", "mult = 2 (default)", "mult = 4"),        col = c("orange", "blue", "darkgreen"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")   ## 3. Pieces and holes: random points on a ring (the empty middle is a hole) and a separate ##    cluster; polypath() shades the region with the hole left open set.seed(1) th <- runif(400, 0, 2*pi); r <- runif(400, 2, 3) pts <- data.frame(x = c(r*cos(th), runif(80, -3, -2)), y = c(r*sin(th), runif(80, 3.5, 4.5))) br <- semiboundary(pts) plot(pts, asp = 1, pch = 16, cex = 0.4) polypath(br, col = adjustcolor("skyblue", 0.4), border = "blue", lwd = 2, rule = "evenodd")  sum(is.na(br$x)) + 1                               # 3 rings: the ring's two edges and the cluster #> [1] 3  # \donttest{ ## Surfaces shown only inside the boundary, with its outline and the data library(ggplot2) outline <- function(b) { b$ring <- cumsum(is.na(b[[1]])); b } data(scallopKnots) fs <- semireg(asinh(tot.catch) ~ s(longitude, latitude, bs = "ztps",                                   xt = list(knots = as.matrix(scallopKnots))), data = scallop) semipred(fs, covariate = c("longitude", "latitude"), boundary = b, trans = sinh)$plt +   geom_path(data = outline(b), aes(longitude, latitude, group = ring), inherit.aes = FALSE,             na.rm = TRUE)   data(copperKnots) fc <- semireg(grade ~ s(xcoord, ycoord, bs = "ztps", xt = list(knots = as.matrix(copperKnots))) +                 s(zcoord, bs = "os"), data = copper) semipred(fc, covariate = c("xcoord", "ycoord"), boundary = b2)$plt +   geom_path(data = outline(b2), aes(xcoord, ycoord, group = ring),             inherit.aes = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +   geom_point(data = holes, aes(xcoord, ycoord), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 0.8)  # boundary = TRUE draws the boundary from the model's data (scale "auto": here "sd") semipred(fc, covariate = c("xcoord", "ycoord"), boundary = TRUE)$plt  # }

Two crossed factors: a common curve and deviation curves for f1, f2 and f1:f2, each ##    with its own variance; which deviations are needed? set.seed(1) dx <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length = 15), f1 = factor(c("p", "q")), f2 = factor(c("u", "v")),                   rep = 1:3) dx$y <- sin(2*pi*dx$x) + (dx$f1 == "q")*sin(pi*dx$x)^2 + rnorm(nrow(dx), 0, 0.2) fx <- semireg(y ~ s(x, f1*f2, bs = "os", k = 6), data = dx) varcomp(fx, test = TRUE) #>                         vcov     SE  2.5 %      97.5 %     LRT   p.value #> s_x_f1_f2.(Intercept) 0.0000     NA 0.0000          NA  0.0000 1.0000000 #> s_x_f2.(Intercept)    0.0005 0.0011 0.0001 191055.5255  0.3757 0.2700000 #> s_x_f1.(Intercept)    0.0532 0.0426 0.0173      0.6851 11.6162 0.0003269 #> s_x.(Intercept)       0.3776 0.2198 0.1559      1.8653  7.1297 0.0037910 #> residual              0.0345 0.0039 0.0280      0.0435      NA        NA #>  #> Tests (likelihood ratio, each row's model refitted): #>   s_x_f1_f2.(Intercept): smooth s_x_f1_f2 dropped; 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>   s_x_f2.(Intercept): smooth s_x_f2 dropped; 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>   s_x_f1.(Intercept): smooth s_x_f1 dropped; 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>   s_x.(Intercept): smooth s_x dropped; 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>  #> Advice: #> ! A variance is estimated as zero (or a correlation as +-1): its interval #>   and SE are not reliable, and 'no variation' is not shown. Test it (test = #>   TRUE) or simplify the random effects. #> i To test a variance against zero use varcomp(test = TRUE): it uses the #>   boundary (mixture or bootstrap) reference, not the naive chi-square, #>   which is conservative.  ## 4. An additive model with a varying coefficient: a smooth in x1, and the effect of z ##    changing smoothly with x2 (numeric 'by') set.seed(2) da <- data.frame(x1 = runif(200), x2 = runif(200), z = rnorm(200)) da$y <- sin(3*da$x1) + da$z*sin(2*pi*da$x2) + rnorm(200, 0, 0.3) fa <- semireg(y ~ s(x1, bs = "os") + s(x2, by = z, bs = "os"), data = da) anova(fa)$smooth #>     term   variance   logLik logLik.without      LRT      p.value #> 1   s_x1 0.03875716 -65.4386      -126.8535 122.8299 7.596575e-29 #> 2 s_x2_z 0.33715120 -65.4386      -159.4806 188.0839 4.164359e-43 #>                        test #> 1 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 2 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1)  ## 5. A basis of your own (checked before the fit): a seasonal cycle on a straight trend set.seed(3) ds <- data.frame(day = 1:730) ds$y <- 10 + 0.002*ds$day + 2*sin(2*pi*ds$day/365) + rnorm(730) season <- function(d) cbind(sin(2*pi*d/365), cos(2*pi*d/365), sin(4*pi*d/365), cos(4*pi*d/365)) fs <- semireg(y ~ day + s(day, bs = "user", xt = list(basis = season, null = "none")),               data = ds) semipred(fs, covariate = "day")$plt  ## 6. A tensor-product surface for two covariates on different scales (data(ozoneCalif)), ##    and a curve in a third data(ozoneCalif) fo <- semireg(ozone ~ t2(inversion.base.height, inversion.base.temp) +                 s(daggett.pressure.gradient, bs = "os", k = 15), data = ozoneCalif) anova(fo)$smooth          # a variance per penalty of the surface #>                                             term  variance    logLik #> 1                    s_daggett_pressure_gradient  4.591269 -1022.055 #> 2 t2_inversion_base_height_inversion_base_temp_1  0.000000 -1022.055 #> 3 t2_inversion_base_height_inversion_base_temp_2  1.124284 -1022.055 #> 4 t2_inversion_base_height_inversion_base_temp_3 12.919219 -1022.055 #>   logLik.without          LRT      p.value                      test #> 1      -1040.213 3.631529e+01 8.392096e-10 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 2      -1022.055 2.169145e-10 4.999941e-01 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 3      -1022.438 7.662851e-01 1.906844e-01 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 4      -1026.259 8.407200e+00 1.868689e-03 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) semipred(fo, covariate = c("inversion.base.height", "inversion.base.temp"))$plt  # \donttest{ ## 7. Binary responses with a random intercept per child (HRW::indonRespir): the probability ##    of a respiratory infection over age if (requireNamespace("HRW", quietly = TRUE)) {   data(indonRespir, package = "HRW")   fb <- semireg(respirInfec ~ s(age, bs = "os", k = 10) + vitAdefic + female + height + stunted +                   visit2 + visit3 + visit4 + visit5 + visit6 + (1 | idnum),                 family = binomial, data = indonRespir)   semipred(fb, "age", "age")$plt }   ## 8. Subject-specific curves: each subject's own straight line, (Days | Subject), and its ##    own spline deviation, one variance for all; are the subjects' curves straight lines? fr <- semireg(Reaction ~ s(Days, bs = "os", k = 4) + (s(Days, k = 4) | Subject),               data = lme4::sleepstudy) anova(fr)$smooth #>             term     variance    logLik logLik.without      LRT      p.value #> 1         s_Days 3.055837e-07 -862.9684      -862.9684  0.00000 1.000000e+00 #> 2 s_Days_Subject 2.251268e+02 -862.9684      -871.7951 17.65343 1.325185e-05 #>                        test #> 1 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #> 2 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1)  ## 9. Curves by group, the price of apartments in Warsaw by district (HRW::WarsawApts) if (requireNamespace("HRW", quietly = TRUE)) {   data(WarsawApts, package = "HRW")   WarsawApts$district <- factor(WarsawApts$district)   fw <- semireg(areaPerMzloty ~ s(construction.date, by = district, bs = "os", k = 15),                 data = WarsawApts)   semipred(fw, "district", "construction.date", contr = c("Srodmiescie", "Mokotow"))$plt   predictmeans(fw, "district", covariate = c(construction.date = 1980))$means } #>      district estimate std.error  df conf.low conf.high group #> 1     Mokotow 130.9225  3.510809 401 124.0207  137.8244    A  #> 2 Srodmiescie 138.2202  8.320780 401 121.8624  154.5780    A  #> 3        Wola 118.9150  3.389961 401 112.2507  125.5794     B #> 4    Zoliborz 131.6012  5.959483 401 119.8854  143.3169    AB # }

code: library(predictmeans) ## Counts with extra zeros: curves of two treatments, a random site effect, a negative ## binomial with zero inflation; the rate ratio of the curves along x and where it differs ## from 1 set.seed(5) cn <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 3, length = 30), trt = factor(c("ctl", "trt")), site = factor(1:8)) cn$y <- rnbinom(nrow(cn), size = 3,                 mu = exp(1 + sin(cn$x) + (cn$trt == "trt")*0.5*cn$x + rnorm(8, 0, 0.3)[cn$site])) cn$y[runif(nrow(cn)) < 0.1] <- 0 fc <- semireg_tmb(y ~ s(x, by = trt, bs = "os", k = 6) + (1 | site), ziformula = ~ 1,                   family = glmmTMB::nbinom2, data = cn) rr <- semipred(fc, "trt", "x", contr = c("trt", "ctl"), band = "simultaneous") #> The model has zero inflation (ziformula ~1): the means are those of the conditional (count) part, mu, as emmeans and predict(type = "conditional") give; the overall mean is (1 - pi) mu, with pi the probability of an extra zero. Ratios are of these means (the same for overall means only when pi is the same). mean_type = "overall" gives the overall means. attr(rr$pred_df, "significant") #>        from to direction #> 1 0.7241379  3         > predictmeans(fc, "trt", covariate = c(x = 1.5))$means #> The model has zero inflation (ziformula ~1): the means are those of the conditional (count) part, mu, as emmeans and predict(type = "conditional") give; the overall mean is (1 - pi) mu, with pi the probability of an extra zero. Ratios are of these means (the same for overall means only when pi is the same). #>   trt estimate std.error  df conf.low conf.high  response response.std.error #> 1 ctl 1.842115 0.1565336 469 1.534521  2.149709  6.309871           0.987707 #> 2 trt 2.852923 0.1517429 469 2.554743  3.151103 17.338385           2.630977 #>   response.conf.low response.conf.high group #> 1          4.639104           8.582363    A  #> 2         12.867989          23.361818     B # \donttest{ ## Repeated measures: curves over time, AR(1) correlation within subjects (the residual ## covariance, dispformula = ~0); means at a time with Satterthwaite df set.seed(7) d <- expand.grid(t = 1:8, id = factor(1:12)) d$A <- factor(rep(c("a1", "a2", "a3"), each = 32)) d$y <- sin(d$t/3) + rnorm(12, 0, 0.4)[d$id] +   unlist(lapply(1:12, function(i) as.numeric(stats::arima.sim(list(ar = 0.6), 8, sd = 0.4)))) d$tf <- factor(d$t) fa <- semireg_tmb(y ~ s(t, by = A, bs = "os", k = 4) + (1 | id) + ar1(tf + 0 | id),                   dispformula = ~0, data = d) predictmeans(fa, "A", covariate = c(t = 4), pairwise = TRUE)$pairs #>   level1 level2   estimate std.error       df  statistic   p.value     p.adj #> 1     a1     a2  0.2777639 0.4349906 13.49640  0.6385516 0.5338012 0.5338012 #> 2     a1     a3 -0.1610702 0.4431463 14.19657 -0.3634695 0.7216096 0.7216096 #> 3     a2     a3 -0.4388341 0.4381514 14.09415 -1.0015583 0.3334431 0.3334431 #>     conf.low conf.high       lsd p.method #> 1 -0.6584747 1.2140026 0.9362386        t #> 2 -1.1102914 0.7881510 0.9492212        t #> 3 -1.3779868 0.5003185 0.9391526        t varcomp(fa) #>                       vcov     SE  2.5 %       97.5 % #> id.(Intercept)      0.0737 0.2157 0.0079 7.077491e+11 #> id.1.var            0.3662 0.2435 0.1376 2.521000e+00 #> cor.id.1            0.7865 0.1441 0.3112 9.470000e-01 #> s_t_Aa1.(Intercept) 0.0244 0.0257 0.0063 1.373100e+00 #> s_t_Aa2.(Intercept) 0.0116 0.0160 0.0024 8.644800e+00 #> s_t_Aa3.(Intercept) 0.0425 0.0452 0.0109 2.558500e+00 #> residual            0.0000     NA 0.0000           NA  ## Binary responses with a random intercept per child (HRW::indonRespir) if (requireNamespace("HRW", quietly = TRUE)) {   data(indonRespir, package = "HRW")   fb <- semireg_tmb(respirInfec ~ s(age, bs = "os", k = 10) + vitAdefic + female + height +                       stunted + visit2 + visit3 + visit4 + visit5 + visit6 + (1 | idnum),                     family = binomial, data = indonRespir)   semipred(fb, "age", "age")$plt }  # }

code: library(predictmeans) Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro) fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety+(1|Block/Variety), data=Oats) varcomp(fm) #>                               vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 % #> Variety:Block.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8754  40.9773  657.7703 #> Block.(Intercept)         214.4810 168.8381  70.8628 2575.3156 #> residual                  177.0831  37.3324 121.8272  280.9241 # is each variance needed? (one refit per row) varcomp(fm, test = TRUE) #>                               vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 %    LRT  p.value #> Variety:Block.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8754  40.9773  657.7703 7.6615 0.002821 #> Block.(Intercept)         214.4810 168.8381  70.8628 2575.3156 4.9782 0.012830 #> residual                  177.0831  37.3324 121.8272  280.9241     NA       NA #>  #> Tests (likelihood ratio, each row's model refitted): #>   Variety:Block.(Intercept): drop (1 | Variety:Block); 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) #>   Block.(Intercept): drop (1 | Block); 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) # \donttest{ # the same by parametric bootstrap (a few seconds; more draws and ncore for real use) varcomp(fm, test = TRUE, test_method = "bootstrap", nboot = 99) #>                               vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 %    LRT p.value #> Variety:Block.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8754  40.9773  657.7703 7.6615    0.01 #> Block.(Intercept)         214.4810 168.8381  70.8628 2575.3156 4.9782    0.02 #> residual                  177.0831  37.3324 121.8272  280.9241     NA      NA #>  #> Tests (likelihood ratio, each row's model refitted): #>   Variety:Block.(Intercept): drop (1 | Variety:Block); parametric bootstrap (99 draws) #>   Block.(Intercept): drop (1 | Block); parametric bootstrap (99 draws) # } # a GLMM: the boundary mixture is conservative here, the bootstrap nearer 5% gm <- glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),             family = binomial, data = lme4::cbpp) varcomp(gm, test = TRUE) #>                    vcov     SE  2.5 % 97.5 %     LRT   p.value #> herd.(Intercept) 0.4125 0.2294 0.1757 1.8476 14.0058 9.112e-05 #>  #> Tests (likelihood ratio, each row's model refitted): #>   herd.(Intercept): drop (1 | herd); 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1) fm1 <- lme(yield ~ nitro*Variety, random=~1|Block/Variety, data=Oats) varcomp(fm1) #>                         vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 % #> Block.(Intercept)   214.4745 168.8318  70.8610 2575.1692 #> Variety.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8756  40.9772  657.7746 #> residual            177.0835  37.3325 121.8275  280.9250 # the same components by the analysis of variance varcomp(aov(yield ~ nitro*Variety + Error(Block/Variety), data=Oats)) #>                   vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 % #> Block         214.4771 168.8340  70.8619 2575.2100 #> Block:Variety 106.0618  67.8755  40.9773  657.7726 #> residual      177.0833  37.3324 121.8274  280.9246  data(Orthodont, package="nlme") mod1 <- lme(distance ~ age, random=~age|Subject, data=Orthodont) varcomp(mod1) #>                            vcov     SE   2.5 %   97.5 % #> Subject.(Intercept)      5.4151 4.9583  1.5819 128.6996 #> Subject.age.(Intercept) -0.3211 0.4244 -0.4943   0.1570 #> Subject.age              0.0513 0.0415  0.0166   0.6844 #> residual                 1.7162 0.3303  1.2163   2.6042 # correlation and variance structures mod2 <- gls(distance ~ age*Sex, correlation=corAR1(form=~1|Subject),             weights=varIdent(form=~1|Sex), data=Orthodont) varcomp(mod2) #>              vcov     SE  2.5 %  97.5 % #> cor.Phi    0.7473 0.0681 0.5815  0.8535 #> var.Female 0.5647 0.0908 0.4121  0.7738 #> residual   9.5035 2.8443 5.7032 18.9234 # the error term of a linear model varcomp(lm(yield ~ Block + nitro*Variety, data=Oats)) #>              vcov      SE    2.5 %   97.5 % #> residual 254.2192 48.4777 180.6923 384.1423

title: predictmeans 2.0.0
text: Estimability checks (means, pairs, empty-cell contrasts, slopes) longer depend units covariate: site mean large units aliased slope reported 0 SE 0. anova() lmer fits: factor nested another data (y ~ G + T) tested within Type III, G/T, caution write G/T; balanced nested designs longer called unbalanced; ML fits get Satterthwaite df message instead Kenward-Roger label; failed Kenward-Roger adjustment Types II III falls back Satterthwaite. pm_slopes() gives pairs slopes equal model (covariate x term interaction). covariatemeans() drew curves data identify (covariate constant within levels factor model, site mean site; function factors). now stops message pointing contr = pm_slopes(), estimate differences curves; single points estimated NA, advice. pm_slopes() gave slope 0 SE 0 covariate aliased factor (site mean site model). slopes now NA, advice; differences kept. slopes table estimable column, means table. autoplot() means group data (data = TRUE) works ggplot2 3.4, DESCRIPTION promises (stopped: “position_jitterdodge() requires least one aesthetic dodge ”). Permutation tests, bootmodels() variance-component tests lmer/glmer fits missing values work older lme4 (1.1-35 dropped missing rows twice refit()). glmmTMB fit aliased coefficients (e.g. combinations levels without data) longer stops every means function “logical subscript long”; means equal lmer ML fit. semireg() deviation smooth s(x, f1*f2) longer gives warning “number items replace”. permlmer() reports lme4 convergence warnings permuted refits , count, instead one warning per refit. Tukey p-values within atvar levels used number pairs instead means. predictmeans() failed lmer models missing treatment combination, ML lmer fits. predictmeans() permlist atvar failed; user Df lmer gave NA p-values. Factor levels containing ":" broke pairwise tables. Within-atvar adjusted p-values matched wrong pairs. contrastmeans() failed missing treatment combination. Kenward-Roger ignored prior weights offsets lmer fits. semireg() 0/1 responses SEs 15-25% small; Gamma inverse-Gaussian SEs small. semireg() gaussian fits wrong anova() df varcomp() SEs. semireg_tmb() negative binomial SEs scaled theta; zero-inflated bands narrow. semipred(contr = ) bands generalized models wrong. varcomp() SEs glmer limits glmmTMB wrong. R2_glmm() wrong glmmTMB families, offsets correlated random effects. permindex() block group returned indices sorted data. permmodels() permuted one column cbind() responses; type lmer tables compared different statistics. permmodels() CookD() refit data set name found elsewhere. CookD() failed every lmer model.
